### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to plakophilin deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.484)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6809371, Reactome:R-HSA-351906, Reactome:R-HSA-6798695)

**Proposed mechanism:** DSP (HGNC:2779) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosome assembly and function (GO:0034772); Desmosome assembly and function (GO:0034772) —LEADS_TO→ Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (HP:0001649); Desmosome assembly and function (GO:0034772) —LEADS_TO→ Woolly hair (HP:0002110); Desmosome assembly and function (GO:0034772) —LEADS_TO→ Keratoderma (HP:0000985); PKP1 (HGNC:9131) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosome assembly and function (GO:0034772); Desmosome assembly and function (GO:0034772) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermolysis bullosa simplex (HP:0007374). Mutations in DSP and PKP1 disrupt the normal assembly and function of desmosomes, a shared cellular structure critical for epidermal and cardiac cell adhesion. This disruption in desmosome function leads to the distinct phenotypes of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, woolly hair, and keratoderma in DSP-deficient individuals, and epidermolysis bullosa simplex in PKP1-deficient individuals.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in DSP in patients diagnosed with EBS-PKP1, or conversely, identification of a pathogenic variant in PKP1 in patients with ACM-WHK, would falsify this hypothesis of distinct genetic origins for the respective diseases, while supporting a shared, albeit complex, genetic etiology.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on desmosomal integrity for both cardiac and epidermal health could reveal common therapeutic targets for disorders affecting these tissues, potentially leading to novel treatment strategies for both ACM-WHK and EBS-PKP1.

#### 2. arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia 9  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.474)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6809371)

**Proposed mechanism:** Desmoplakin (HGNC:2731) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosome assembly (GO:0034772); Plakophilin 2 (HGNC:9020) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosome assembly (GO:0034772); Desmosome assembly (GO:0034772) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cardiomyocyte structure (HP:0005000); Abnormal cardiomyocyte structure (HP:0005000) —LEADS_TO→ Arrhythmia (HP:0011414); Desmosome assembly (GO:0034772) —LEADS_TO→ Keratoderma (HP:0000985); Desmosome assembly (GO:0034772) —LEADS_TO→ Woolly hair (HP:0008072). Loss-of-function mutations in DSP and PKP2 disrupt the assembly of desmosomes, leading to abnormal cardiomyocyte structure and function (arrhythmia), as well as skin phenotypes like keratoderma and woolly hair.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in DSP or PKP2 in individuals with both arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with wooly hair and keratoderma and arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia 9, or identification of distinct pathogenic variants in genes unrelated to desmosome function for each disease. _(variant: Common variants (AF > 0.01) in the coding regions of DSP or PKP2.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of desmosome assembly in these distinct but related conditions could lead to targeted therapies for cardiac and skin manifestations, potentially involving stabilization of desmosome function or mitigation of downstream cellular damage.
